title: ECB Confirms 2027 Ashes Schedule as Southampton Gets First Men's Test
excerpt: The five-Test men's series opens at Trent Bridge on June 18, with the women's Ashes running concurrently and a packed summer featuring a WTC final at The Oval.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Men's Ashes 2027 starts June 18 at Trent Bridge, with Southampton hosting its first men's Test.
  • Women's Ashes begin June 24 at Headingley, marking the venue's first women's Test since 2001.
  • WTC final at The Oval starts June 9, with England hosting through 2031.
  • England's summer includes ODI series against Pakistan and New Zealand, plus a Test against Bangladesh.

The England and Wales Cricket Board on Thursday confirmed the full international schedule for England's 2027 home summer, headlined by three Ashes series across men's and women's cricket and the ICC World Test Championship final at The Oval.

https://x.com/mufaddal_vohra/status/2080218290501362085

The five-Test men's Ashes series opens at Trent Bridge, Nottingham on June 18, with matches following at Lord's (June 30), Edgbaston (July 8), the Utilita Bowl in Southampton (July 21), and the Kia Oval (July 29 to August 2). Southampton's inclusion is historic — the venue has never before hosted a men's Ashes Test, expanding the roster of grounds to have staged cricket's oldest international rivalry.

Men's and Women's Ashes Run Side by Side

Following the model set in 2023, the men's and women's Ashes will run concurrently next summer. The ECB said the overlapping format boosted crowds for women's fixtures during the last home Ashes and helped set attendance records.

The women's multi-format series begins with a Test match at Headingley on June 24, the first women's Ashes Test at the Leeds venue since 2001. Three T20 internationals follow at Trent Bridge (July 3), the Kia Oval (July 6), and Emirates Old Trafford (July 9), before three ODIs at Southampton (July 13), Lord's (July 16), and Edgbaston (July 20).

"The last time Australia were here made for captivating cricket, in a way that only the Ashes can provide, as both of our Men's and Women's teams fought back to level the series in dramatic circumstances."

— Richard Gould, ECB Chief Executive Officer

Gould added that the 2027 summer would see the men's team play a Rothesay Ashes Test at the Utilita Bowl for the first time, while the women's team returns to Headingley for an Ashes Test after a gap of more than two decades.

WTC Final and a Packed Calendar

England's summer begins well before the Ashes. The men's team hosts Pakistan in a five-match ODI series starting at Southampton on May 15, followed by a one-off Test against Bangladesh at Lord's from May 28 to June 1.

The ICC World Test Championship final is set for June 9 at the Kia Oval. The ECB confirmed that England will host the WTC final again in 2029 and 2031, making The Oval the sport's premier neutral venue for Test championship deciders. The season closes with New Zealand touring for three T20Is and five ODIs in September, while the women's team plays Bangladesh in three T20Is and three ODIs during the same window.

![The Oval. WTC final at The Oval starts June 9, with England hosting through 2031.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/bc/The_Kia_Oval_-_geograph.org.uk_-_4645561.jpg)

Long-Term Venue Allocations Through 2031

The ECB's announcement also outlined venue allocations through 2031, including, for the first time, long-term planning for women's international fixtures alongside men's. India's 2029 five-Test tour will visit Lord's, The Oval, Edgbaston, Old Trafford, and The Ageas Bowl. The next home Ashes in 2031 will be played at Lord's, The Oval, Emirates Old Trafford, Headingley, and Trent Bridge, with the women's series featuring a Test at The Ageas Bowl.

For Indian cricket fans based in the UK, the early confirmation of India's 2029 tour venues offers valuable lead time for planning around what is typically one of the most sought-after ticket allocations in English cricket.

Packed Summer Schedule
›WTC final at The Oval on June 9
›ODI series against Pakistan starting May 15
›One-off Test against Bangladesh from May 28 to June 1
›New Zealand series in September

What's Next

Australia retained the Ashes in the 2025-26 series down under, and England will be looking to reclaim the urn on home soil. Ticket sale dates and broadcast details for the 2027 summer have not yet been announced. The WTC final participants will depend on the current cycle standings, with India and Australia among the leading contenders for a place at The Oval in June.
